tasks.short: Study blueprints and specifications, look up earlier similar jobs, plan the sequence of operations, and write the process sheet.

steps.what: Tool and die maker studies blueprints, sketches, models or specifications
Tool and die maker looks up earlier similar jobs in paper folders
Tool and die maker plans sequences of operations for fabricating the tool or die
Tool and die maker writes the process sheet: by hand today; after the change as a routing in the ERP by picking standard operations with times from earlier jobs and writing the special instructions
Tool and die maker checks the final routing: operations, machines, times and instructions against the planned sequence
Tool and die maker releases the checked routing for the tool job

tasks.design: Drawings and process sheets of finished jobs are stored in the product data system ({OTHER}) by part family, so earlier similar jobs are found by search instead of in paper folders. The process sheet is built as a routing in the ERP ({ERP}) by picking standard operations per machine, with times from earlier jobs; the tool and die maker writes the special instructions, checks the routing and releases it once. Studying drawings and planning the sequence stay with the tool and die maker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Earlier jobs sat in paper folders and process sheets were written by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Product data systems search drawings by part family; ERP routings hold standard operations.
tasks.still_hard: Old jobs are only on paper.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which order of operations avoids distortion.

evidence.claim: Product data systems can store drawings and process sheets by part family and search them.

assumptions: Boundary: from the new job to the process sheet written; making the tool is outside.
Input contract: finished jobs stored with drawings; fallback is paper folders.

Studying, planning, the routing check and the release keep their full time. s2 keeps 40 for reading the found jobs and for old jobs only on paper; s4 keeps 60 because standard operations and times are picked and the special instructions are still written.

incremental.description: Tool and die maker files finished jobs with their part family.

approvals.approved_version: The routing with operations, machines, times and special instructions exactly as checked by the tool and die maker in s4b, released once in {ERP} for this tool job; any change needs a new check and release.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many earlier jobs are only on paper and few operations are standard, so most searching and writing stay (5.9); high: finished jobs stored and standard operations cover most routings (13.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review part requirements, look up material properties, select the metal, and check whether the grade is in stock.

steps.what: Tool and die maker reviews the part's requirements for hardness, wear and heat
Tool and die maker looks up material properties in handbooks and supplier datasheets
Tool and die maker selects metals based on properties such as hardness or heat tolerance
Tool and die maker checks the material rack for the grade and size

tasks.design: A material table ({OTHER}) lists the shop's tool steels and alloys with hardness, toughness, heat tolerance and heat treatment, and filters by required properties, so the tool and die maker does not search handbooks and datasheets. The ERP ({ERP}) shows which grades and sizes are on the rack, so the rack is checked only to pick the bar. Choosing the metal stays with the tool and die maker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Properties were looked up in handbooks and stock checked at the rack.
tasks.enabler_now: Material tables filter by property; ERP holds bar stock by grade and size.
tasks.still_hard: Supplier grades with the same name differ.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which steel cracks in this shop's heat treatment.

evidence.claim: Material tables can filter tool steels by hardness, toughness and heat tolerance.

assumptions: Boundary: from the tool design to stock checked; buying material is outside.
Input contract: material table kept by the workshop lead; fallback is handbooks.
Reviewing requirements and choosing the metal keep their full time. s2 keeps 40 for reading the filtered table and checking supplier grades; s4 keeps 40 because the bar is still picked at the rack.
Bar stock is booked in the ERP when cut.

incremental.description: Tool and die maker books cut bar lengths in the ERP.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many jobs use unusual alloys outside the table and cut bars are not booked reliably, so handbooks and rack checks stay for half of the jobs (10.0); high: standard tool steels in the table and stock booked when cut (23.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Study the part and process, design the jig or fixture, draw up the parts list, and test the jig with first parts.

steps.what: Tool and die maker studies the part and how it is produced
Tool and die maker designs jigs, fixtures and templates on paper sketches
Tool and die maker draws up the parts list for standard components
Tool and die maker tests the jig with first parts and adjusts it

tasks.design: Jigs and fixtures are designed in CAD ({OTHER}) with a library of standard clamps, locating pins and bushes from supplier catalogues and earlier fixtures, so common parts are placed instead of drawn. The parts list is generated from the model. Studying the part and testing the jig stay with the tool and die maker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Jigs were sketched on paper and parts lists written by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: CAD libraries hold standard fixture components and generate parts lists.
tasks.human_edge: Designing a fixture an operator cannot load the wrong way.

reach.learn: Whether jigs are quick to use.

evidence.claim: CAD systems hold libraries of standard fixture components and generate parts lists from the model.

assumptions: Boundary: from the work aid request to the jig proven; series production is outside.
Input contract: CAD licence and component library; fallback is sketches.
Studying the part and testing keep their full time. s2 keeps 70 because standard clamps, pins and bushes are placed and the rest is still designed; s3 keeps 40 for checking the generated parts list.

incremental.description: Tool and die maker adds new fixtures to the library.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly custom one-off fixtures with odd locators, so the library places few parts (9.5); high: families of similar fixtures (20.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Analyse the part drawing, model the tool in CAD, calculate strip layout, forces and clearances, make drawings and the parts list, and review the design with production.

steps.what: Tool and die maker analyses the part drawing and requirements
Tool and die maker develops and designs new tools and dies using CAD
Tool and die maker calculates strip layout, forces and clearances in a spreadsheet
Tool and die maker makes detail drawings and the parts list
Tool and die maker reviews the design with production

tasks.design: Die sets, punches, guide pillars and springs come from suppliers' standard component libraries in the CAD system ({OTHER}), so they are placed instead of modelled. Strip layout, cutting forces and clearances are calculated by the CAD die design module with standard formulas instead of a spreadsheet. Detail drawings and the parts list are generated from the 3D model. Analysing the part, designing the tool and reviewing with production stay with the tool and die maker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Standard parts were modelled by hand and calculations kept in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: CAD die design modules hold standard components and formulas.
tasks.still_hard: Progressive dies with many stations need careful manual layout.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing where a die will wear first.

reach.learn: Whether new dies run without rework.

evidence.claim: KISSsoft Gears module calculates gear types to ISO, DIN, AGMA and VDI standards with sizing tools.
CAD die design modules can calculate strip layout, cutting forces and clearances with standard formulas.

assumptions: Boundary: from the part drawing to the design reviewed; making the die is outside.
Input contract: CAD with die design module licensed; fallback is spreadsheets.

Analysing the part, design decisions and the review keep their full time. s2 keeps 80 because only placing standard components is faster; s3 keeps 40 for checking the module's values; s4 keeps 50 for checking and finishing the generated drawings.
research_questions: Do design errors found at tryout fall?

incremental.description: Tool and die maker keeps component libraries current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: complex progressive dies need careful manual layout, so the module helps less (13.0); high: simple blanking dies with standard sets (25.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The tool and die maker keeps studying drawings, planning, choosing metals and designing tools; paper folders, handbooks, hand-drawn standard parts and spreadsheet calculations shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A tool and die maker with more time at the machine.
